description: Sensors, analogue vs digital signals, logic gates with truth tables, and key components.
content_html:
Analogue and Digital Signals

Electronic systems process information as signals. There are two types: analogue signals vary continuously — like the voltage from a thermistor that rises and falls as temperature changes. Digital signals have only two states: HIGH (logic 1) or LOW (logic 0). A button that is either pressed or not pressed produces a digital signal.

Most sensors produce analogue outputs. To use an analogue sensor with a digital circuit (such as a microcontroller), an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) is needed. The ADC samples the voltage at regular intervals and converts it into a binary number. Without an ADC, the microcontroller cannot read the sensor. Examiner reports show that half of students leave ADC questions blank — memorising this definition is a guaranteed mark.

Key Fact

An ADC (analogue-to-digital converter) converts a continuous analogue voltage into a digital binary number that a microcontroller or processor can read. Sensors that produce analogue outputs (LDR, thermistor, microphone) all need an ADC to interface with digital control systems.

Sensors

Sensors are input devices that convert a physical quantity into an electrical signal. The two most common in engineering exams are:

  • LDR (light-dependent resistor) — its resistance decreases as light intensity increases. In bright light: low resistance → high current. In the dark: high resistance → low current. Used in automatic street lighting, security systems and photocopiers.
  • Thermistor — its resistance decreases as temperature increases (NTC type — negative temperature coefficient). Used in thermostats, engine management systems and fire alarms. A thermistor in a potential divider circuit produces an analogue voltage that changes with temperature.

Other sensors include pressure sensors (transducers), proximity sensors (inductive or capacitive), and sound/vibration sensors (microphones, piezo sensors). All produce an electrical signal proportional to the physical quantity they measure.

Logic Gates

Logic gates are the fundamental building blocks of digital electronic circuits. Each gate has one or more binary inputs (1 or 0) and produces a single binary output determined by a logical rule. You must be able to name the gate, draw its symbol and complete its truth table.

AND gate: output is HIGH only when ALL inputs are HIGH. Rule: “both A AND B must be 1 for output to be 1.”

ABOutput

OR gate: output is HIGH if ANY input is HIGH. Rule: “A OR B (or both) is 1 for output to be 1.”

ABOutput
000
011

111

NOT gate (inverter): single input, single output — output is always the opposite of the input.

InputOutput
01
10

NAND gate = AND + NOT. Output is LOW only when ALL inputs are HIGH; otherwise HIGH. It is the inverse of AND. NAND gates are the most common gate in integrated circuits — any logic function can be built from NAND gates alone.

NOR gate = OR + NOT. Output is HIGH only when ALL inputs are LOW; otherwise LOW. The inverse of OR. Like NAND, any logic function can be built from NOR gates alone.

XOR gate (exclusive OR): output is HIGH only when inputs are DIFFERENT (one is 0 and the other is 1). When both inputs are the same (both 0 or both 1), output is LOW. Used in comparator circuits and error-detection systems.

Passive Components: Resistors, Capacitors and Diodes

You must be able to identify these components by their circuit symbols and describe their function:

  • Fixed resistor — limits current in a circuit. Symbol: rectangular box (BS 3939 UK) or zigzag. Value in ohms (Ω). Used in series with LEDs to prevent burnout.
  • Variable resistor (rheostat) — a resistor whose value can be adjusted mechanically. Used in dimmer switches, volume controls and sensor potential dividers. Symbol: rectangular box with an arrow through it.
  • Capacitor — stores electrical charge. Polarised capacitors (electrolytic) must be connected the correct way round; non-polarised capacitors can be connected either way. Used for smoothing rectified DC and as timing components.
  • Diode — allows current to flow in one direction only. The triangle symbol points in the direction of conventional current flow; the bar is the cathode (negative terminal). Signal diodes are small and fast; rectifying diodes handle larger currents in PSU circuits.
  • LED (light-emitting diode) — a diode that emits light when current flows through it. Must be connected the correct way round (longer leg = anode = positive). Always used with a series resistor to limit current. Output devices in control panels and status indicators.
Key Fact

Common exam error: students identify a transistor symbol as a resistor. A resistor symbol is a box (or zigzag). A transistor symbol has three connections — collector, base and emitter — with an arrow on the emitter. A diode symbol is a triangle pointing to a bar. Memorise these three symbols and you eliminate a common source of lost marks.
exam_tip_html: For logic-gate questions, always draw a truth table — don’t try to work out the output in your head. Start with all combinations of inputs (00, 01, 10, 11 for two inputs) and apply the gate rule to each row. The most common error is confusing AND (both must be 1) with OR (at least one must be 1). For component identification questions, look carefully at the number of connections: a resistor has two, a transistor has three, an LED has two but one leg is longer. Name the component precisely — “a part that controls current” will not earn the identification mark.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Analogue signals vary continuously (e.g. thermistor, LDR); digital signals have only two states (HIGH/LOW). An ADC converts analogue sensor outputs into digital numbers for a microcontroller to process.
  • AND gate output is HIGH only when all inputs are HIGH; OR gate output is HIGH when any input is HIGH; NOT gate inverts the input. NAND, NOR and XOR are their combinations and inversions.
  • Key components: fixed and variable resistors limit current; capacitors store charge and smooth DC; diodes allow current in one direction only; LEDs emit light when forward-biased and always need a series resistor.

practice_questions.text:
A student sees a component in a circuit diagram. It has three connections, with an arrow on one of them pointing outward.

Identify the component.
practice_questions.marks:
Transistor (NPN transistor) [1 mark]
Note: 'resistor' is a common wrong answer — resistors have two connections and are shown as a box or zigzag.

practice_questions.text:
Complete the truth table for an AND gate:

A | B | Output
0 | 0 | ___
0 | 1 | ___
1 | 0 | ___
1 | 1 | ___
practice_questions.marks:
0 | 0 | 0 [correct]
0 | 1 | 0 [correct]
1 | 0 | 0 [correct]
1 | 1 | 1 [correct]
1 marks awarded for each pair correct:
- Rows 1 and 2 correct [1 mark]
- Row 3 correct [1 mark]
- Row 4 correct [1 mark]
[3 marks total — must use 0 and 1 not yes/no or true/false]

practice_questions.text: Explain the difference between an analogue signal and a digital signal. Give one example of a sensor that produces each type.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct point, up to 2 marks:
- Analogue signal: varies continuously between two values, can take any value (e.g. thermistor output, LDR output, microphone output).
- Digital signal: has only two states — HIGH (1) or LOW (0) (e.g. push-button switch, reed switch, digital encoder output).
[2 marks — must distinguish 'continuous range' vs 'two states' and give a valid example for each]

practice_questions.text:
A security alarm system uses two sensors: a door sensor (input A) and a motion sensor (input B). The alarm should sound only when both sensors are triggered at the same time.

(a) Name the logic gate that should be used.
(b) Complete the truth table for this system.
(c) Explain why an OR gate would not be suitable.
practice_questions.type: 4 marks — Describe Stages of a Process
practice_questions.marks:
(a) AND gate [1 mark]
(b) Truth table:
A=0,B=0 → 0; A=0,B=1 → 0; A=1,B=0 → 0; A=1,B=1 → 1 [1 mark for all rows correct]
(c) An OR gate output is HIGH when either A OR B is triggered alone — the alarm would sound even if only one sensor is triggered, causing false alarms. [2 marks — 1 for identifying OR would activate on a single sensor, 1 for linking to the consequence (false alarms)]
[4 marks total]

practice_questions.text: State the function of an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) and explain where it is positioned in a programmable electronic system.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct point, up to 2 marks:
- An ADC converts a continuous analogue voltage (from a sensor) into a discrete digital binary number.
- It is placed between the analogue sensor and the microcontroller/digital processor, so that the sensor output can be read by the digital system.
[2 marks]

practice_questions.text:
Fenwick Electronic Systems Ltd is designing a temperature-monitoring unit for a food refrigeration cabinet. The unit must trigger an alarm if the temperature rises above 5°C. The system uses a thermistor, an ADC, a microcontroller and a buzzer.

Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using a thermistor as the temperature-sensing element for this application. In your answer, consider at least one alternative sensor.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Evaluate an Engineering Decision
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8): Explains how a thermistor (NTC) produces an analogue voltage that decreases as resistance falls with rising temperature; this must be converted by an ADC before the microcontroller can process it. Evaluates advantages (cheap, small, robust, wide temperature range, fast response). Evaluates disadvantages (non-linear response — resistance doesn't drop proportionally with temperature, requires calibration; analogue output needs ADC). Considers an alternative (digital temperature sensor IC such as DS18B20): direct digital output (no ADC needed), pre-calibrated, higher accuracy. Compares on cost, accuracy, integration complexity and food-safety regulatory context. Justified conclusion.

Secure (5-6): Correct description of thermistor function, at least two advantages and one disadvantage, one alternative with brief comparison. Conclusion present.

Developing (3-4): Basic description of thermistor. One advantage and one disadvantage. Limited alternative.

Emerging (1-2): Simple identification of thermistor with minimal reasoning.

[8 marks]

options: Converts a digital signal into an analogue voltage
Converts a continuous analogue voltage into a digital binary number

knowledge_checks.q: A light-dependent resistor (LDR) has a _____ resistance when light intensity is high.
A NOT gate has a single input and produces an output that is always _____ of the input.
Match each logic gate to its rule:
right: Output is HIGH only when ALL inputs are HIGH
Output is HIGH when ANY input is HIGH
Output is HIGH only when inputs are DIFFERENT

flashcard_questions.a: A signal that can take any value within a continuous range, varying smoothly with the quantity it measures.
A signal with only two states: HIGH (1) or LOW (0).
Converts a continuous analogue voltage into a digital binary number for a microcontroller to read.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the output of an OR gate when both inputs are 0?
What is the output of an AND gate when inputs are 1 and 1?
If a NAND gate sees inputs 1 and 1, what output does it produce?
flashcard_questions.a: 0 — both inputs HIGH gives a NAND output of LOW (0).
A light-dependent resistor — its resistance decreases as light intensity increases.
A thermistor whose resistance decreases as temperature increases (negative temperature coefficient).
A semiconductor component that allows current to flow in one direction only.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must an LED always be connected with a series resistor?
flashcard_questions.a: To limit the current and prevent the LED from burning out.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a capacitor do in a circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: Stores electrical charge; used for smoothing rectified DC and as a timing component.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an XOR gate's output when both inputs are the same?
flashcard_questions.a: 0 (LOW) — XOR output is HIGH only when inputs are different.

glossary_terms.definition: Signals that can take any value within a continuous range, such as the output voltage from a temperature sensor varying smoothly with temperature.
Signals that can only have two states: HIGH (1) or LOW (0), represented by specific voltage levels such as 5 V and 0 V.
A circuit that converts a continuous analogue voltage into a discrete digital number that a microcontroller or processor can read.
An electronic component that stores charge and blocks DC but passes AC; used for smoothing, timing and coupling in circuits.
A semiconductor device that allows current to flow in one direction only; used in rectifier circuits and as protection components.
